title: Mean and Median
text: The arithmetic mean is the sum of values divided by their count. The median is the middle value after observations are ordered, or the average of the two middle values when the count is even. Extreme values can move the mean more than the median.

title: Variance and Standard Deviation
text: Variance is the average squared deviation of observations from their mean. Standard deviation is the square root of variance and is expressed in the original units of the observations.

title: Sampling Bias
text: A sample is biased when its selection process systematically favors some members of a population over others. Increasing the size of a biased sample does not by itself remove that systematic error.

title: Ecological Niches
text: An ecological niche describes the conditions and resources a species uses and its interactions with other organisms. Two species with strongly overlapping niches may compete for limiting resources.

title: Ecological Succession
text: Ecological succession is a sequence of changes in a community's species composition over time. Primary succession begins where soil is absent, while secondary succession follows disturbance where soil remains.

title: Trophic Levels
text: A trophic level is an organism's feeding position in a food chain or web. Producers form the base by making organic matter, and consumers obtain energy by eating organisms or organic matter.

title: Cosmological Redshift
text: Cosmological redshift stretches light to longer wavelengths as space expands while the light travels. For distant galaxies, redshift is used to infer recession and study cosmic expansion.

title: Transit Method for Exoplanets
text: The transit method detects an exoplanet when it passes in front of its star and causes a small, repeated dip in the star's observed brightness. The dip's depth is related to the planet-to-star size ratio.

title: Stellar Spectra
text: A star's spectrum contains absorption or emission lines at characteristic wavelengths. These lines reveal chemical elements and can also provide information about temperature and motion.

title: Opportunity Cost
text: Opportunity cost is the value of the best alternative forgone when a choice is made. It includes relevant benefits sacrificed, even when no money changes hands.

title: Price Elasticity of Demand
text: Price elasticity of demand measures how responsive quantity demanded is to a change in price. Demand is called elastic when the percentage change in quantity demanded is larger than the percentage change in price.

title: Public Goods
text: A public good is non-rival when one person's use does not reduce availability to others, and non-excludable when people cannot readily be prevented from using it. These properties can make voluntary private provision difficult.
